title: Exchange Argument

story.briefing: One repair bay, a queue of jobs. Every job that waits costs the Core, so the order you choose decides the total bill.
story.success: Queue reordered. The total waiting cost drops to its minimum.

description: A single bay processes jobs one after another, and you may choose the order. Each job takes a given number of cycles. A job finishing time is the moment its own processing ends, counting from zero. Return the smallest possible total of all finishing times. An empty list returns 0.
hints: A job placed early adds its duration to the finishing time of every job after it. So the cost of a job depends on how many jobs still follow it.
Swap any two adjacent jobs and compare the totals — that comparison tells you which order is better, and it is the same answer every time. This is the standard way to justify a greedy rule.
Sort the durations ascending and run them in that order. Keep a running elapsed time, adding each duration to it and adding the new elapsed time to the total.
